confusions: The skill says to use the template's examples for a missing setting, but the catalogue shows empty examples for most templates; I used the template rule params as given

Template limits for CONV-040 say a 30-statement limit blocks rewrites of legacy objects on a blocking policy, but gives no way to phase in a limit (e.g. a higher start value), so the choice of 30 vs a looser limit was left to me

The recipe for code review says to create each template as its own policy, but also says to put extra rules in one policy of my own; it does not say whether a single-template recipe should also get its own policy when the ask only covers some of its parts
The catalogue's CHG-001 template uses object_kinds query only; the ask says no tests in general, so I widened it to function, which I could not confirm is the intended default
Policy files carry no tags in my final version: I dropped tags I could not confirm exist in the workspace
wished_for: A template or check for try/catch around database writes, or for error handling on every outbound statement at once
Guidance on how to phase in a size limit (advisory warn level, or a stepped max) for codebases with existing long functions
A recipe note on which parts of a recipe to skip when the request covers only some of them
Working examples for tests that check they pass, not just that they exist
why_confidence: Three checks map directly to the named complaints (error handling, tests, size), and all three parse with no rule warnings. But the ask also covers 'you know the drill' and 200-line functions as lines, and tests are only checked for existence. The policies reduce the review noise, but do not prevent prod breakage by themselves.
